why: The student fills the bound with a.length - 1 and justifies it only as 'the last index', showing no model of the pairwise swap: iterating past the midpoint re-swaps every pair and leaves the array essentially unreversed (and i < a.length-1 even skips nothing useful). Correctly glossing a.length-1 as the last index is a lexical fact, not a grasp of the loop-bound concept being assessed, so the applied rule ('visit every element to reverse') is a documented wrong rule, placing it at L0 rather than L1.
